clue.text: Help to back an ethnic group and there'll be a tirade

indicators.note: to back is to run in reverse, so the word for help is read from right to left

parts.note: to aid is to help
a tribe is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: Supporting a particular people is sure to provoke an angry outburst from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns AID into DIA, which comes before TRIBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a long, bitter verbal attack.

clue.text: Deny one's trapped by the fuzz!

indicators.note: one's is held inside the word for fuzz

parts.note: down is soft fluffy fuzz, as on a peach
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone protests innocence after being caught by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate or refuse to acknowledge something as your own.

clue.text: A man taking in over-weight and belligerent woman

indicators.note: the man takes in the turned weight unit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turned over means the abbreviation for weight is reversed

parts.note: OZ is the abbreviation for ounce, a weight

explanation.surface: A fellow eats too much and becomes a battling female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns OZ into ZO, which goes inside MAN after A.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Amazons were a race of women warriors, hence a strong, combative female.

clue.text: Regret shown about church decoration

indicators.note: the word for regret goes around the church abbreviation

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Sorrow is expressed about the church's ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill or pleated strip of fabric used to trim a garment.

clue.text: Part with one bird only to get another

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Separate from a single bird just to acquire a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a marsh bird of the heron family, so it is another bird after the tern.

clue.text: The Quaker allowed to pass by the guard

definitions.text: allowed to pass by the guard

explanation.surface: A member of the Society of Friends is waved through by a sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends; a sentry's challenge 'Who goes there?' is answered with this word to be let through.
explanation.definitionFit: A Quaker is formally called this, and a sentry lets through someone who is no enemy.

clue.text: Re-establish control over the body politic

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the control word above the body politic

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
the state is the nation as an organised political community

explanation.surface: Restoring authority over the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore to a former position, to put back.

clue.text: Looks on minerals as horrible things

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
ores are minerals from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: Someone regards mining products as ugly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly sights that offend the eye, such as blots on a landscape.

clue.text: Discharge a public school admitted in time

indicators.note: the school letters are let into the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton is an English public (private fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A school lets in someone on time to fire a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge an explosive is to set it off.

clue.text: Mark an urban area's need of resources

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
a city is a large urban area; the 's is a link meaning 'has'

explanation.surface: A city is described as blighted by its shortage of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage of supplies is a lack, the condition where there is not enough to go round.

clue.text: Order, given unlimited credit

indicators.note: set free of its usual limits, the word credit is let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A command comes with an open-ended line of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct someone is to tell them what to do, to command.

clue.text: Notes about the French decline

indicators.note: the two notes sit about the French article

parts.note: F and G are musical notes
la is French for the (feminine)

explanation.surface: Musical notes about the French are falling away.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or weaken, to wane.

clue.text: Not the kind of bread to use when preparing a snack!

definitions.text: Not the kind of bread to use when preparing a snack!

parts.words: Not the kind of bread to use when preparing a snack
parts.note: a snack is by definition something less than a full meal, so the joke is that a bread named for a complete meal cannot belong in one

explanation.surface: Advice on which loaf to avoid when making a light bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread made from flour that keeps the entire grain is named this way.

clue.text: Demonstrated how to go in opposite directions

indicators.note: the word how is placed so that it goes in between the two compass letters

parts.note: south and north are opposite compass points, S and N
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was shown the way to set off two ways at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed or exhibited has been made visible, the past participle of a verb meaning display.

clue.text: A boy with nothing inside him as it's early

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the boy, him being that boy

parts.note: a son is a male child, a boy
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: An empty-headed lad is said to be ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean before long, in a short while.

clue.text: A clothier striking a craftsman

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a fitter is a skilled mechanic who assembles parts

explanation.surface: A tailor out on strike is a skilled worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop that supplies clothes and equipment, a seller of garments.

clue.text: The last home, by the way, may well be most grim

parts.note: a grave is a person's final resting place
ST is short for street, a way; 'by' places it beside the first piece

explanation.surface: A tomb beside a road is the bleakest of sights.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of serious, used of a situation as worst or most solemn.

clue.text: The Moors made use of iron possible

indicators.note: the letters of The Moors are used and made into something new

explanation.surface: North African conquerors employed metal where they could.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is one possible device for flattening creases.

clue.text: Attractive binding

explanation.surface: A charming commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming describes something winning; engaging can also mean committing or pledging, as in a binding promise.

clue.text: A dragon of a medico -awfully stern

parts.note: MO is the Medical Officer, a doctor

indicators.note: an awful jumble of the word stern rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A doctor who is fearsomely severe in manner, a real dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges STERN into NSTER, which follows MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fabulous beast, an example of a fearsome creature.

clue.text: Criticise the bar

explanation.surface: Finding fault with a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly; a rail is also a horizontal rod.

clue.text: Come across, right?

explanation.surface: A question asking whether encountering someone is proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter someone is to come across them; as an old adjective it means fitting or proper.

clue.text: Drink is made by Irving's brother

parts.note: taken as written
Ira is a man's name, here someone's brother

explanation.surface: A beverage produced by a relative of a man named Irving.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from the Atlantic island of the same name is a drink.

clue.text: Strive to make music

explanation.surface: Make an effort to play a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to make great effort; a strain is also a passage of melody.

clue.text: Keep a hundred-least possible

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the word least shuffles its letters

explanation.surface: Hold on to a hundred at the very minimum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges LEAST into ASTLE, after C. 'Keep' is a noun, the stronghold of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a medieval stronghold.

clue.text: Animals in a nature reserve look a picture of health

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters across these words

explanation.surface: The creatures kept on a wildlife reserve are glowing with good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'lOOK A PIcture'; the rest of the clue is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal of central Africa, related to the giraffe; the plural is the same word.

clue.text: Drink from tin — an idea if drunk!

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger about and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take a beverage straight out of a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if drunk' shuffles TIN AN IDEA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brew made from leaves grown on the subcontinent, such as Assam or Darjeeling, is a beverage.

clue.text: Bill and Edward were working

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Edward were on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to function or perform, so acted means operated or were working.

clue.text: Crowds around international leader, and that gives a boost

indicators.note: the crowds wrap round the letter that follows

parts.note: hosts are great numbers, crowds

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Throngs gather round a world statesman, giving him a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoists are lifting devices, and to lift something is to raise it up.

clue.text: Many is the brochure written to beguile

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a large number
taken as written
a tract is a short pamphlet or brochure

explanation.surface: Lots of people have the leaflet written to charm them.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to divert someone's attention, to lure it elsewhere.

clue.text: Watch some soldiers draw back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: to draw back is read here as the word drag running in reverse

parts.note: to drag is to draw or pull

explanation.surface: Observe a squad of troops pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAG into GARD, after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at attentively, to observe.

clue.text: Sound steps taken to provide entertainment

definitions.text: Sound steps taken to provide entertainment

parts.words: Sound steps taken to provide entertainment
parts.note: the steps are not prudent measures but noisy footwork, metal-tipped shoes clicking for an audience

explanation.surface: Sensible measures are adopted to amuse people.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage dance with metal-tipped shoes makes rhythmic noise with each step.
